catalyst_text: Received Health Canada approval for pediatric atopic dermatitis
detailed_catalyst_text: Health Canada approved roflumilast cream 0.05% for the topical treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in children 2 to 5 years of age. The approval was supported by the pivotal Phase 3 INTEGUMENT-PED trial and a long-term extension showing consistent safety through 56 weeks. This expands treatment options with a once-daily, steroid-free therapy for preschool-aged children.
catalyst_text_evidence: Arcutis Canada, Inc., a commercial stage company focused on delivering meaningful innovations in immuno-dermatology, today announced that Health Canada has approved PrZORYVE (roflumilast) cream 0.05% for the topical treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis (AD) in pediatric patients 2 to 5 years of age. Health Canada's approval is supported by data from the pivotal Phase 3 INTEGUMENT-PED study, which met its primary and key secondary endpoints, demonstrating significant improvements in overall disease severity, with treatment benefits observed as early as Week 1. In the long-term extension study, ZORYVE cream 0.05% demonstrated a consistent safety profile through 56 weeks, supporting its use in the long-term management of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis.

catalyst_text: sNDA accepted PDUFA set for February 23 2027
detailed_catalyst_text: FDA accepted a supplemental NDA to expand use of the 0.05% cream in mild to moderate atopic dermatitis to include infants 3 to 24 months. Acceptance initiates formal review and a PDUFA target action date of 2027-02-23 was assigned, marking regulatory progress for this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: "Arcutis Biotherapeutics, Inc. ... today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has accepted its supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) for ZORYVE (roflumilast) cream 0.05% to expand the indication for the topical treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis to include infants aged 3 to 24 months." "The FDA has set a PDUFA target action date of 2027-02-23."

catalyst_text: Received FDA approval for pediatric indication expansion
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA approved a supplemental application expanding the 0.3% cream indication to treat plaque psoriasis, including intertriginous areas, in children aged 2 years and older. This extends the prior label from ages 6 and up and provides the first once‑daily non‑steroidal topical option for this young pediatric population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Arcutis Biotherapeutics, Inc. today announced that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has approved the supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) to expand the indication for ZORYVE (roflumilast) cream 0.3% for the topical treatment of plaque psoriasis, including intertriginous areas, to children down to age 2. ZORYVE cream 0.3% was previously approved for the treatment of plaque psoriasis in adults and children down to age 6. ZORYVE cream 0.3% is the first once-daily, non-steroidal therapy approved for children with plaque psoriasis as young as 2 years of age.

catalyst_text: Submitted sNDA supported by positive infant study data
detailed_catalyst_text: An sNDA was submitted to the FDA to expand the indication of roflumilast cream 0.05% to include mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in infants aged 3 months to less than 24 months. The filing is supported by Phase 1 pharmacokinetic and Phase 2 open-label study data in infants showing favorable tolerability and efficacy. This could broaden access to a non-steroidal topical option for a vulnerable pediatric population if subsequently approved.
catalyst_text_evidence: WESTLAKE VILLAGE, Calif., 2026-04-27 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Arcutis Biotherapeutics, Inc. today announced the submission of a supplemental New Drug Application (sNDA) to the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) seeking to expand the indication for ZORYVE (roflumilast) cream 0.05% to include the topical treatment of mild to moderate atopic dermatitis in infants down to 3 months. The sNDA is supported by positive results from a Phase 1 open-label pharmacokinetic (PK) trial and a Phase 2 open-label trial (INTEGUMENT-INFANT), both of which evaluated once-daily ZORYVE cream 0.05% in infants aged 3 months to less than 24 months with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 data in seborrheic dermatitis
detailed_catalyst_text: An e-poster with a STRATUM Phase 3 subgroup analysis showed the 0.3% foam was well tolerated and improved signs and symptoms through 8 weeks, including in patients with face and/or scalp involvement. These results support use on anatomical areas where topical steroid safety limits their use.
catalyst_text_evidence: Findings from a STRATUM Phase 3 trial subgroup analysis (e-poster) show that ZORYVE foam 0.3% was well tolerated and improved signs and symptoms of seborrheic dermatitis through 8 weeks of treatment in individuals with seborrheic dermatitis including those with face and/or scalp involvement. The analysis supports ZORYVE foam 0.3% as a suitable potential treatment of anatomical areas where topical steroid use is limited by safety considerations, such as the face.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 data in pediatric dermatitis
detailed_catalyst_text: A poster presented new results from the INTEGUMENT-OLE Phase 3 trial in children aged 2 to 5 years with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis, showing the 0.05% cream was well tolerated and produced durable, long-term improvements in caregiver-reported outcomes. These data reinforce sustained benefit and safety in this pediatric age group. The findings add to the totality of clinical evidence for the formulation.
catalyst_text_evidence: New results from the INTEGUMENT-OLE Phase 3 trial (poster presentation) demonstrate that ZORYVE cream 0.05% was well tolerated and provided durable improvements in caregiver-reported outcomes that are maintained over the long term in children aged 2 to 5 years with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis. These follow the recent publication of the full results of INTEGUMENT-OLE published in the journal Pediatric Dermatology earlier this month.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 data in plaque psoriasis
detailed_catalyst_text: Further analyses presented from the Phase 3 ARRECTOR program showed the 0.3% foam improved psoriasis severity versus vehicle, reducing PASI total and component scores. Benefits were seen across multiple anatomical regions, supporting consistent efficacy across the body.
catalyst_text_evidence: Further analysis from the previously published Phase 3 DERMIS-1/2 and ARRECTOR trials (e-poster) found that ZORYVE cream 0.3% and foam 0.3% improved psoriasis severity, reducing Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) total and component scores more than vehicle cream or vehicle foam. Mean improvements in psoriasis were reported with ZORYVE cream and foam across body regions: head and neck, trunk, and upper and lower extremities.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 data in plaque psoriasis
detailed_catalyst_text: Further analyses presented from the Phase 3 DERMIS-1/2 program showed the 0.3% cream improved psoriasis severity versus vehicle, reducing PASI total and component scores. Mean improvements were observed across head/neck, trunk, and extremities, reinforcing efficacy across body regions.
catalyst_text_evidence: Further analysis from the previously published Phase 3 DERMIS-1/2 and ARRECTOR trials (e-poster) found that ZORYVE cream 0.3% and foam 0.3% improved psoriasis severity, reducing Psoriasis Area and Severity Index (PASI) total and component scores more than vehicle cream or vehicle foam. Mean improvements in psoriasis were reported with ZORYVE cream and foam across body regions: head and neck, trunk, and upper and lower extremities.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 2 data in pediatric eczema
detailed_catalyst_text: New clinical results from the INTEGUMENT-INFANT Phase 2 open-label trial in infants 3 months to under 24 months with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis were presented, showing efficacy across multiple endpoints and favorable tolerability. Outcomes included vIGA-AD success, strong EASI-75 responses by Week 4, and rapid caregiver-reported itch improvement, with minimal application-site irritation. These data expand evidence for use in the youngest pediatric population.
catalyst_text_evidence: Arcutis Biotherapeutics, Inc. today announced new data from the INTEGUMENT-INFANT Phase 2 trial demonstrating that ZORYVE (roflumilast) cream 0.05% reduced signs and symptoms of atopic dermatitis, the most common form of eczema, in infants aged 3 months to less than 24 months with mild to moderate atopic dermatitis. The results were presented today during a late-breaking podium presentation at the 2026 American Academy of Dermatology (AAD) Annual Meeting in Denver, CO. In new data released today, among participants who completed four weeks of treatment (n=96), 34.4% achieved Validated Investigator Global Assessment for Atopic Dermatitis (vIGA-AD) success (defined as a score of 0 (Clear) or 1 (Almost Clear) with a ≥2-grade improvement). As previously reported, 58.3% of infants achieved at least a 75% reduction in Eczema Area and Severity Index (EASI-75) at Week 4 (n=96), and 34% of infants at Week 2 (n=100). Furthermore, 66.7% of infants achieved at least a 25% improvement from baseline in pruritus based on the Dynamic Pruritus Scale (DPS-25) at four hours (n=87), 58.6% at one hour (n=87), and 46.6% at 10 minutes (n=88).

catalyst_text: Announced positive topline results from Phase 2 trial
detailed_catalyst_text: Reported positive topline data from the INTEGUMENT-INFANT Phase 2 open-label study in infants aged 3 months to less than 24 months with atopic dermatitis. At Week 4, 58% achieved EASI-75 and the treatment was well tolerated with only mild to moderate adverse events. These results provide evidence of efficacy and tolerability in very young pediatric patients.
catalyst_text_evidence: WESTLAKE VILLAGE, Calif., 2026-02-02 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Arcutis Biotherapeutics, Inc. (NASDAQ:ARQT), a commercial-stage biopharmaceutical company focused on developing meaningful innovations in immuno-dermatology, today announced positive topline results from the INTEGUMENT-INFANT Phase 2 study evaluating the safety, tolerability, and efficacy of ZORYVE (roflumilast) cream 0.05% in infants aged 3 months to less than 24 months with atopic dermatitis. ZORYVE cream, a highly selective and potent topical phosphodiesterase 4 (PDE4) inhibitor, was well tolerated with a safety profile consistent with previous ZORYVE clinical trials. Overall, the incidence of adverse events was low, with all being mild to moderate in severity. ZORYVE cream improved the severity of disease and reduced the area of skin affected by atopic dermatitis, with 58% of participants achieving EASI-75 at Week 4.
